name: Dominion Energy, Inc.
employees: ~15,200 full-time at December 31, 2025, of which ~6,700 at Virginia Electric and Power Company (FY2025 Form 10-K)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Dominion Energy Virginia is the regulated gatekeeper for the largest data-center cluster in the world, and it is being acquired: contracted data-center capacity stood at about 53.8 GW in July 2026 (12.0 GW under firm electric service agreements, 9.4 GW under construction authorizations, 32.4 GW at the substation-engineering stage) against an all-time system peak of 24,678 MW; a new GS-5 rate class with 14-year contracts and 85 percent transmission-and-distribution minimums takes effect on January 1, 2027; a $64.7B five-year capital plan is 25 percent transmission and 18 percent new gas; and on May 15, 2026 the company agreed to an all-stock combination with NextEra Energy that its shareholders vote on today, September 3, 2026, with closing expected in the second half of 2027. BACKGROUND. Richmond, Virginia; NYSE: D. Per the FY2025 Form 10-K the company serves approximately 4.1 million primarily electric utility customers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina with approximately 30.7 GW of generating capacity, 10,800 miles of transmission and 80,400 miles of distribution; Virginia Electric and Power Company (Dominion Energy Virginia) serves approximately 2.8 million customers in Virginia and North Carolina, and data centers were 28 percent of its electricity sales in 2025 (26 percent in 2024). FY2025 operating earnings were $3.42 per share on operating revenue of $16,506M; 2026 guidance is $3.45–$3.69. The Virginia State Corporation Commission set Dominion Energy Virginia's rates in a biennial review whose final order of November 25, 2025 authorized a 9.8 percent return on equity, approved $565.7M and $209.9M of base-rate increases for 2026 and 2027, created the GS-5 class and certified the 944 MW Chesterfield Energy Reliability Center for 2029. The 2025 Integrated Resource Plan Update forecasts demand in the PJM DOM Zone rising 6.3 percent a year over the next decade and more than doubling by 2045; its preferred plan adds 17,534 MW of solar, 3,460 MW of wind, 2,000 MW of storage, 1,944 MW of small modular reactors and 8,510 MW of gas by 2045. Collection gap: the standalone GS-5 rate sheet, the collateral quantum in dollars per megawatt and the SCC's final-order text were not reachable; the ramp, exit-fee and notice terms below rest on the SCC's own fact sheet and the company's investor deck, with secondary summaries flagged where used.
ecosystemRole: We assess Dominion Energy Virginia as the entity whose calendar, not any customer's, decides when Loudoun County's campuses get power — the substation-engineering, construction-authorization and electric-service-agreement ladder it publishes is the sequence every hyperscaler and colocation operator in this file that builds in Northern Virginia is standing in. Basis: the company's own Data Center Requests page and investor decks, the 2022 eastern-Loudoun transmission pause and the 500/230 kV Reliability Loop now being built to end it, and the SCC's February 2026 record of roughly 70,000 MW of pending requests. For the storage and power-equipment sellers in this corpus it is three different counterparties at once: a statutory buyer of storage and solar through an annual solicitation cycle (a Virginia law of April 2026 mandates 4.0 GW of short-duration storage by 2030 and 16.0 GW by 2045); a self-builder of gas, transmission and offshore wind recovered through riders; and the utility whose tariff terms — the GS-5 minimums, the direct-assignment of transmission costs ordered in July 2026 — set the economics of every behind-the-meter bridge-power and buffering project on its system. Per the merger releases, after the NextEra combination closes Dominion Energy Virginia keeps its president and its dockets, but supplier qualification is likely to be read against NextEra's platform.

productsAndServices.name: Regulated retail electric service — Dominion Energy Virginia, and the GS-5 large-load rate class
productsAndServices.description: Virginia Electric and Power Company serves approximately 2.8 million residential, commercial, high-load, industrial and governmental customers across about 30,000 square miles of Virginia and northeastern North Carolina, per the FY2025 Form 10-K and the 2025 IRP Update, which also states that customers have uninterrupted power 99.98 percent of the time excluding major storms and that residential rates are approximately 9 percent below the national average. The 'high load' revenue class is defined in the 10-K and 10-Q as customers with actual or anticipated demand of 25 MW or higher and an annual load factor of 75 percent or higher; data centers were 28 percent of Virginia Power's electricity sales in 2025. Rates are reset in a biennial review before the SCC: the November 25, 2025 final order in Case PUR-2025-00058 approved base-rate increases of $565.7M for 2026 and $209.9M for 2027 against $822M and $345M requested, authorized a 9.8 percent return on equity against 10.4 percent requested, and created the GS-5 class. Per the company's Q4 2025 investor deck, GS-5 applies to all existing and new customers with measured or contracted demand of 25 MW or greater on contiguous sites and a load factor of at least 75 percent; minimum demand charges are the higher of usage or 85 percent of contracted capacity for transmission and distribution and 60 percent for generation, in place as long as service is provided, with customers who began service before 2016 exempt; new electric service agreements from January 1, 2027 carry a 14-year term (a four-year ramp plus ten years, then automatic one-year renewals), exit fees equal to the remaining minimum obligations, cash deposits for equipment orders and enhanced collateral. The SCC's February 2026 fact sheet adds that customers without sufficient credit may be required to guarantee funds covering up to 60 percent of their minimum charges over the contract term.
highlights: The SCC's own words on the order: certain large-scale customers 'will be required to pay a minimum of 85% of contracted distribution and transmission demand, and 60% of generation demand, among other requirements', effective January 1, 2027
The 10-K states the purpose plainly: the 14-year contract, collateral and demand minimums 'are designed to minimize both cross-rate class subsidies and stranded costs'

The same order directed Dominion to file alternative cost-allocation proposals for generation and transmission and to submit its large-load interconnection process for SCC review by February 2, 2026 — the filing that disclosed roughly 70,000 MW of pending requests (Virginia Business)

A follow-on order of July 31, 2026 in the Rider T-1 case (PUR-2026-00056) requires direct assignment of defined transmission facilities to data centers through mandatory contributions in aid of construction, with an amended line-extension policy due within 90 days (Utility Dive)

Secondary summaries of the order (Compute Law Blog, Arcadia) add a ramp of up to four years at a minimum of 20 percent of contracted demand per year and a three-year notice to reduce load — not verified against the order text
productsAndServices.positioning: The GS-5 class sits with AEP Ohio's 2025 data-center tariff (85 percent minimum after a ramp, 12-year terms) and Georgia Power's 100 MW rules as the templates the guidance literature calls the national norm; Dominion's version is distinctive for its separate, lower generation minimum, its 14-year term and its application to existing as well as new customers above 25 MW.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Tariff service under SCC-approved rate schedules; large loads contract through an electric service agreement negotiated with the company's Data Center Team.
targetSegments: Hyperscale and colocation data centers in Loudoun, Prince William, Henrico, Chesterfield and Stafford counties
Residential, commercial and industrial customers in Virginia and northeastern North Carolina
productsAndServices.roadmap: GS-5 effective for new agreements January 1, 2027; alternative cost-allocation proposals and the amended line-extension policy in 2026 proceedings; the third biennial review is due to be filed in March 2027 with a final order late 2027 (company deck).

productsAndServices.name: Large-load interconnection — the data-center connection process
productsAndServices.description: Per the company's Data Center Requests page, a request begins with a site plan, a load letter and a load-ramp schedule, followed by short- and long-term power plans, infrastructure design, right-of-way acquisition, permitting and material procurement, a regulatory filing where required, and construction; loads under 50 MW 'can typically utilize existing distribution infrastructure and require 1-2 years to complete', while loads over 50 MW 'will most likely require the extension of transmission lines and the construction of a new substation', with bridging solutions to allow commissioning and initial load while the final plan is built. The investor deck formalizes the contract ladder: a Substation Engineering Letter of Authorization (a detailed engineering plan with costs reimbursed to Dominion), a Construction Letter of Authorization (which authorizes construction, with the customer obliged to reimburse all spent costs should it walk away) and an Electric Service Agreement (which 'includes revenue requirement whether customer takes service or not'). Contracted capacity across the three stages was about 53.8 GW in July 2026 — 12.0 GW under ESAs, 9.4 GW under CLOAs and 32.4 GW under SELOAs — up from 48.5 GW in December 2025, 40.2 GW in December 2024 and 16.5 GW in July 2023. The company connected 15 data centers (977 MW) in 2024 and 11 (744 MW) in 2025 and expects 13 in 2026; it received 118 delivery-point requests for 26.0 GW in 2025 alone, 409 requests for about 67 GW since 2020, and serves over 450 data centers from more than 50 customers.
highlights: Firm demand is the smaller tranche: ESAs and CLOAs together were about 21 GW at year-end 2025 with another 27 GW in engineering, and the deck states that existing ESAs alone cover projected demand growth through 2036
The 2025 IRP Update counted 16,913 MW under executed ESAs or CLOAs as of July 31, 2025 and 30,132 MW under study at the engineering stage

Requests have outrun connections by an order of magnitude — 26.0 GW requested in 2025 against 744 MW connected — which is the arithmetic behind the GS-5 minimums and the deposit and reimbursement clauses

Eastern Loudoun County has been transmission-constrained since 2022; Dominion said then that most planned development would receive a reduced allocation of anticipated power through January 2026, and Equinix's 2026 Ashburn expansion still cited Dominion's upgrades as a gating factor (Hoodline)
Customer quality is a stated selling point: 82 percent of data-center customers investment-grade and 76 percent with relationships of ten years or more (Q4 2025 deck)
productsAndServices.positioning: No other utility in this corpus publishes a three-stage contracted-capacity ladder each quarter; the closest comparators are AEP's and ERCOT's request queues, which the guidance literature treats as conversation openers rather than demand. Dominion's ESA tranche is the nearest thing to certified demand a seller can read.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct engagement through the Data Center Team and the company's work-request portal; costs of engineering and construction are borne by the customer under the SELOA and CLOA.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers building in Northern and Central Virginia
Colocation developers (Equinix, STACK, Vantage and others named in the sources)
Any load of 25 MW or more on a contiguous site
productsAndServices.roadmap: 13 connections expected in 2026; the interconnection process filed for SCC review on February 2, 2026; Loudoun Reliability Loop lines energizing summer 2026 through 2028 (company pages).

productsAndServices.name: Dispatchable generation build — Chesterfield Energy Reliability Center and the gas program
productsAndServices.description: The Chesterfield Energy Reliability Center is described on the company's project page as up to 1,000 MW from four natural-gas simple-cycle turbines of up to 250 MW each on the Chesterfield Power Station property, with construction beginning in 2026 and operations in 2029; the FY2025 10-K carries it as a 944 MW simple-cycle station expected to cost approximately $1.5 billion and enter service in 2029. The SCC granted the certificate and a rate adjustment clause in its November 25, 2025 order (POWER reported the CPCN application of March 3, 2025 at $1.47 billion construction cost, fuels including gas blended with up to 10 percent hydrogen and distillate, and six 3,500 kW black-start generators), suspended the order in December 2025 on a reconsideration petition, reinstated it in February 2026, and the approval was appealed to the Supreme Court of Virginia on May 27, 2026 (SELC). The Q4 2025 investor deck lists the wider program as 'CT: 2029; 2 CCGTs: 2032—2034 — ~6.5 GW of capacity ✓Turbines secured' in Virginia and a CT in 2028 plus a CCGT in 2032–2033 (~1.3 GW) in South Carolina, with new gas generation 18 percent of the $65B five-year plan. A 2026 Dispatchable Generation RFP was issued July 1, 2026 with bids due December 18, 2026.
highlights: The 2025 IRP Update's preferred plan adds 8,510 MW of gas by 2045 — four 1,466 MW combined-cycle blocks and three 882 MW combustion turbines in the model, the first CT in 2032 and the first CC in 2033 — and states that combined-cycle units 'were selected the first year they were made available in all primary Portfolios'

The SCC's certificate order, as summarized by ReisingerGooch, cited 'actual and projected demand growth in PJM and increases in PJM capacity prices'; the plan itself notes the DOM Zone cleared just over $329/MW-day for 2026/2027
The preferred plan would require a VCEA reliability exception to keep existing and planned fossil generation from retiring in 2045 (2025 IRP Update)
Turbine supply is secured for the committed 6.5 GW per the deck; the turbine OEM for CERC is not named on any first-party page and the GE 7FA.05 attribution seen in a search snippet was not verified
productsAndServices.positioning: Alongside Entergy's Meta-funded plants and Georgia Power's certified combined cycles, Dominion's gas build is the mid-Atlantic instance of the guidance literature's 'massive gas procurement' move; its distinctive feature is that it is being litigated under a clean-energy statute rather than simply certified.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility-owned and rider-recovered (Rider CERC); equipment procured through the company's EPC and turbine supply agreements; the 2026 RFP solicits third-party dispatchable proposals.
targetSegments: System capacity and reliability for the DOM Zone
productsAndServices.roadmap: CERC in service 2029 (court challenge pending); CCGTs 2032–2034; 2026 Dispatchable Generation RFP bids December 18, 2026; the next comprehensive IRP is due in an even-numbered year per the company's own filing cadence.

productsAndServices.name: Solar, storage and renewable procurement — the VCEA program and the annual RFPs
productsAndServices.description: Per the 2025 IRP Update, 'to support the development of renewable and energy storage resources, the Company annually issues requests for proposal ('RFPs') for new solar (utility-scale and distributed), energy storage' and related resources, and it 'continues to self-develop energy storage resources and solicits energy storage PPAs in annual RFPs'. The company's RFP page lists a 2026 Acquisition RFP (Virginia; utility-scale and distributed solar, onshore wind, solar-plus-storage, wind-plus-storage and stand-alone energy storage; webinar June 18, 2026) and a 2026 PPA RFP issuing October 1, 2026 for Virginia and North Carolina; the 2025 PPA RFP closed February 9, 2026. The October 2025 clean-energy petition (Case PUR-2025-00148) sought six utility-scale solar projects totaling about 845 MW, two energy storage projects totaling about 155 MW and purchase agreements for ten solar facilities totaling 439 MW, described in the Q3 2025 deck as $2.9B of new investment; per the Q2 2026 10-Q the SCC approved four solar projects (about 532 MW) and one storage project (about 80 MW) for approximately $1.5 billion, in service between 2028 and 2030. The 10-K states that Virginia Power 'plans to invest approximately $2.0 billion from 2026 to 2030 to develop battery-storage facilities'. The statutory frame moved in April 2026: the 10-Q records a Virginia law requiring 16.0 GW of short-duration storage by the end of 2045 including 4.0 GW by the end of 2030, and 4.0 GW of long-duration storage by 2045 including 2.0 GW by 2035 — replacing the VCEA's 2.7 GW-by-2035 storage finding.
highlights: Utility-owned storage in service or approved is still small: pilots of 12 MW (Scott Solar), 2 MW (New Kent) and 2 MW (Hanover) totaling 56 MWh, Dry Bridge 20 MW, a 50 MW Dulles airport project, 28.34 MW of the 30 MW pilot allowance approved, and about 700 MW petitioned in the 2025 plan (company pages; IRP)

The 2025 IRP Update's preferred plan carries 2,000 MW of storage through 2045 (1,300 MW company-owned, 700 MW under PPAs) — down from about 4,500 MW in the 2024 IRP — while the April 2026 statute requires 4,000 MW by 2030; the next comprehensive plan has to reconcile the two

Solar is the volume line: 17,534 MW in the preferred plan, a VCEA target of 6.5 GW of utility-owned solar by 2030 described as on track, and named projects including Randolph (800 MW, phased 2030–2032) and Honeybee (300 MW, 2029)
The 2025 IRP Update reports a long-duration pilot testing a four-hour zinc-halide battery and an iron-air battery capable of discharging for up to 100 hours
The SCC's 2025 order on the 2024 IRP directed the company to analyze raising its battery-storage build limits in future plans (WHRO)
productsAndServices.positioning: Among the regulated storage buyers the guidance literature compares — Georgia Power's certified 3,022.5 MW, Entergy's first standalone RFP, PSO/SWEPCO's all-source solicitations — Dominion is the one with a standing annual cycle and a statutory floor; the self-build slice is EPC-mediated, and no battery integrator or cell supplier for any Dominion project is named on a first-party page.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Two lanes: PPAs awarded to developers bidding the annual PPA RFP (the developer chooses the equipment), and utility-owned projects bid into the Acquisition RFP and built through EPC and supply agreements the company signs.
targetSegments: Independent developers bidding Virginia and North Carolina PPAs
Project sellers offering mechanically complete solar and storage assets
The company's own rider-recovered storage fleet
productsAndServices.roadmap: 2026 PPA RFP issues October 1, 2026; 4.0 GW short-duration storage mandate by end-2030; approved 80 MW storage in service 2028–2030; $2.0B of storage capital 2026–2030.

productsAndServices.name: Electric transmission — the Loudoun Reliability Loop, the 765 kV backbone and the Heritage–Mosby HVDC link
productsAndServices.description: Electric transmission is the largest line in the 2026–2030 capital plan: $13.9B for Dominion Energy Virginia plus $1.0B for the Valley Link joint venture, 25 percent of the $65B total per the Q4 2025 deck, largely rider-recovered. The company's Northern Virginia program page describes a new 500/230 kV loop near Ashburn in three projects: Mars–Wishing Star (SCC-approved April 2023, to be energized by summer 2026), Aspen–Golden (approved February 5, 2025, affirmed by the Supreme Court of Virginia February 19, 2026, in service June 2028) and Golden–Mars (Route 3A approved 2026, construction summer 2026 to summer 2028), with the Golden–Mars FAQ stating the loop 'is required by the regional grid organization (PJM)' because of high-tech-sector demand. Further west, Morrisville–Wishing Star adds a 36.5-mile 500 kV line through Fauquier, Prince William and Loudoun (SCC application February 27, 2026; in service summer 2030) and Line 514 rebuilds a 3.5-mile 500/230 kV corridor into Leesburg (application May 21, 2026; 2031). PJM's February 2025 selections gave Dominion, AEP and FirstEnergy a jointly developed 765 kV backbone — 260 miles from Putnam County, West Virginia to Frederick County, Maryland and 155 miles from Campbell County to Fauquier County, Virginia — and PJM's board approved on February 12, 2026 an $11.84B window including Dominion's Heritage–Mosby project: a bipolar ±525 kV HVDC link of about 185 miles, fully underground, with a capability of 3,000 MW and a required in-service date of June 1, 2032, at $2,271.7M for the line plus $773.7M and $745.4M for the two converter stations (PJM board whitepaper); the company summarized the window as a portfolio 'totaling over ~$5.0B'.
highlights: Eastern Loudoun's constraint dates to 2022, when Dominion said the growth was 'resulting in transmission constraints in a pocket of eastern Loudoun County that primarily serves large customers' and Data Center Frontier reported reduced power allocations through January 2026

The 2026–2030 plan puts 20 percent of capital into transmission at the consolidated level; Dominion Energy Virginia's system counts over 6,700 miles of transmission lines and more than 800 substation assets (SVP bio)

PJM's own report on the 2027/2028 capacity auction noted that a delayed 500 kV backbone line 'significantly impacted MAAC, SWMAAC and DOM CETLs' — transmission timing already moves the capacity price the utility's customers pay

The SCC rejected an underground alternative for Golden–Mars that Loudoun Now reported at $1.5 billion, three times the overhead cost; PJM received numerous public comments asking it to defer the HVDC decision
productsAndServices.positioning: The corpus's other transmission owners (AEP, FirstEnergy, Exelon's utilities) appear only as PJM co-awardees; Dominion is the transmission owner for the corridor where the load is, which is why its lines carry the corridor's connection dates.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility-owned and recovered through the electric transmission rider (Rider T-1) — the rider the SCC ordered in July 2026 to be re-cut so that defined facilities are directly assigned to large loads.
targetSegments: Data Center Alley load pockets in Loudoun and Prince William
productsAndServices.roadmap: Mars–Wishing Star summer 2026; Aspen–Golden and Golden–Mars 2028; Morrisville–Wishing Star 2030; Line 514 2031; Heritage–Mosby HVDC June 2032; 765 kV projects without a firm timeframe per the company.

productsAndServices.name: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind (CVOW)
productsAndServices.description: A 2.6 GW, 176-turbine wind farm 27 to 44 miles off Virginia Beach, per the company's February 2025 cost release, using Siemens Gamesa turbines of the same model as the Moray West project; a 50 percent noncontrolling interest was sold to Stonepeak in October 2024 (Q2 2026 10-Q). Per the Q2 2026 investor deck the project was about 81 percent complete at July 31, 2026, with all 176 monopiles and transition pieces installed, 31 turbines completed, two of three offshore substations commissioned and the third expected by year-end 2026; the budget stood at $11.65B including contingency (from $9.8B originally, $10.7B in February 2025 and $11.4B in Q1 2026), project-to-date investment was about $9.8B, and the final turbine is now expected at year-end 2027 after earlier guidance of end-2026 and then early 2027. The first electrons — about 14.7 MW — reached the grid on March 23, 2026 (coastalvawind.com). The FY2025 10-K describes the customer cost-sharing bands: Virginia Power recovers 50 percent of incremental cost between $10.3 billion and $11.3 billion and none between $11.3 billion and $13.7 billion.
highlights: The deck's updated levelized cost is $83/MWh in 2027 dollars against a legislative prudency cap of $149/MWh; the SCC's July 2025 rider order approved $670M of annual revenue and the July 2026 Rider OSW order set a residential impact of $0.90 a month (ReisingerGooch)

The U.S. Department of the Interior issued a 90-day stop-work order on December 22, 2025; Dominion called it a threat to grid reliability and won a preliminary injunction in the Eastern District of Virginia on January 16, 2026 (offshorewind.biz)

Tariffs that became effective in April 2026, revised PJM network-upgrade costs and updated installation projections drove the Q2 2026 budget, per the 10-Q, which carries the project at approximately $11.7 billion excluding financing
Offshore wind is under 2 percent of the five-year capital plan; Dominion's remaining funding obligation was about $1.0B at mid-2026 with Stonepeak funding 48 percent of the remaining capital (deck)
productsAndServices.positioning: The only utility-owned, rate-based offshore wind farm of its size in the United States; its cost history is the reference case for what the regulated model can carry against federal and tariff headwinds.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility-owned with a 50 percent financial partner; recovered through Rider OSW under the VCEA's public-interest finding.
targetSegments: VCEA offshore-wind compliance (5,200 MW state target by 2034)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Third offshore substation year-end 2026; 144 turbines remaining at July 31, 2026; final turbine year-end 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Nuclear fleet and small modular reactor development at North Anna
productsAndServices.description: Dominion operates seven nuclear units in three states under its Chief Nuclear Officer (company bio): Surry Units 1 and 2 (licensed through May 2052 and January 2053), North Anna Units 1 and 2 (each about 945 MW, per the company's station page), Millstone in Connecticut and V.C. Summer in South Carolina. Nuclear relicensing is 7 percent of the five-year plan ($4.4B for Dominion Energy Virginia). On SMRs, the 2025 IRP Update states that units are 'typically around 300 MW per unit', that the company filed its first Rider SMR in November 2024 to recover early-stage development costs at North Anna and that the SCC approved it in July 2025, and that following a July 2024 RFP the company 'continues to analyze the feasibility of siting one or more SMRs at the North Anna Power Station' and to 'explore opportunities for innovative financial partnerships with third parties and high load customers'. The preferred plan includes six SMRs (1,944 MW) in its outer years; the station page says the first could be operational 'by the early-to-mid 2030s'. On July 14, 2026 the company filed to renew North Anna's Early Site Permit for 20 years beyond its November 2027 expiry and placed the North Anna 3 construction-and-operating license in deferred status, stating it has 'not made any commitments' to build (World Nuclear News).
highlights: Amazon and Dominion Energy Virginia signed a memorandum of understanding on October 16, 2024 'to explore innovative new development structures' for SMR development at North Anna; Utility Dive reported the aim as at least 300 MW of new capacity
The IRP records that SMRs 'are essential for ensuring reliability' in every primary portfolio and that large-scale nuclear was selected only in the forced-retirement portfolio
The NextEra combination requires Nuclear Regulatory Commission approval of the license transfers for the fleet, per the merger release and the Q2 2026 10-Q
productsAndServices.positioning: Among the nuclear owners in this corpus Constellation sells clean-firm attributes to hyperscalers from a merchant fleet; Dominion's fleet is rate-based and its SMR work is the regulated-utility version of the same bet, financed through a rider and a hyperscaler partnership rather than a PPA.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Rate-based generation; SMR development costs through Rider SMR; partnership structures with high-load customers under exploration.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers seeking clean firm supply in Virginia
productsAndServices.roadmap: ESP renewal decision pending at the NRC; first SMR early-to-mid 2030s per the company; six SMRs in the plan through 2045.

productsAndServices.name: Dominion Energy South Carolina and Contracted Energy
productsAndServices.description: Dominion Energy South Carolina serves approximately 0.8 million electric and 0.5 million natural-gas customers (FY2025 10-K), with its own biennial-style rate proceedings, a 2028 combustion turbine and a 2032–2033 combined cycle (~1.3 GW, turbines secured) in the capital plan, and $7.6B of 2026–2030 capital. Contracted Energy holds Millstone Power Station, long-term contracted solar assets and a renewable natural gas portfolio, per the Chief Nuclear Officer's bio; the 2026 guidance midpoint of $3.57 includes $0.07 per share of RNG 45Z income.
highlights: South Carolina customer growth ran at 2.0 percent year to date in 2026 against 0.9 percent in Virginia (Q2 2026 deck)
The combined company after the NextEra transaction keeps an operational headquarters for Dominion Energy South Carolina in Cayce (merger release)
productsAndServices.positioning: Context for the consolidated financials rather than a data-center franchise; the AI-load story is Virginia's.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Regulated tariff service (electric and gas) and contracted output.
productsAndServices.roadmap: South Carolina CT 2028 and CCGT 2032–2033; merger hearings before the South Carolina PSC December 8, 2026.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Dominion's data-center pipeline is firm in its smallest tranche and speculative in its largest, and that the company's own instruments are built to keep it that way. Basis: per the Q2 2026 investor deck, 12.0 GW of the 53.8 GW is under electric service agreements that 'include revenue requirement whether customer takes service or not', 9.4 GW under construction authorizations with full cost reimbursement on walk-away, and 32.4 GW at the engineering stage; the February 2026 SCC filing counted about 70,000 MW of requests against a 24,678 MW peak, with 45,000 MW carrying no connection date; connections have run at 11 to 15 a year for a decade against 118 requests in 2025 alone. The GS-5 minimums from January 2027 and the deposit and reimbursement clauses are the filter. We expect the engineering tranche to convert slowly and the annual connection count — not the gigawatt headline — to remain the measure of throughput.

(High confidence) We assess that wires, not generation, are the binding constraint on Northern Virginia load through at least 2028 and in places through 2032, and that this sustains the behind-the-meter bridge-power market on Dominion's system for the rest of the decade. Basis: the 2022 eastern-Loudoun pause with reduced allocations through January 2026 (Data Center Frontier); the Reliability Loop's dates — Mars–Wishing Star summer 2026, Aspen–Golden and Golden–Mars 2028 — with Morrisville–Wishing Star in 2030, Line 514 in 2031 and the Heritage–Mosby HVDC link in June 2032; transmission at 25 percent of the $65B plan; Equinix's 2026 filing still citing Dominion's upgrades as a gating factor; and PJM's own note that a delayed 500 kV backbone moved the DOM Zone's import limits in the 2027/2028 auction.

(High confidence) We assess that Dominion's storage procurement is a statutory machine with two lanes, and that the utility-owned lane is the smaller and more EPC-mediated of the two. Basis: the annual PPA and Acquisition RFPs the IRP describes; the October 2025 petition's 155 MW of owned storage against 439 MW of solar PPAs; the 10-K's $2.0B of storage capital over 2026–2030 (3 percent of the plan); pilots and approvals in the tens of megawatts; and the fact that no battery integrator or cell maker appears on any first-party page. For a storage seller the addressable Virginia market is the developer bidding the October 1, 2026 PPA RFP and the utility's approved-vendor list — in that order.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the 2025 IRP Update and the April 2026 storage statute are in open conflict and that the next comprehensive plan will raise the storage build. Basis: the Update's preferred plan carries 2,000 MW of storage through 2045 and no generic storage build before 2030, down from about 4,500 MW in the 2024 plan; the SCC's July 2025 order had already directed analysis of higher battery-storage build limits; the 10-Q records a law requiring 4.0 GW of short-duration storage by the end of 2030 and 16.0 GW by 2045. The reconciliation could also come through PPAs rather than rate-based plant, which would move the volume to the developer lane rather than the utility's own. Collection gap: no SCC action on the 2025 Update and no final order on the 2025 clean-energy petition were found.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that gas is the company's firm-capacity answer and that it is legally exposed in a way its solar and storage programs are not. Basis: the Chesterfield certificate was granted, suspended, reinstated and then appealed to the Supreme Court of Virginia within six months; the preferred plan adds 8,510 MW of gas and would require a VCEA reliability exception to keep fossil units past 2045; the company reports its committed 6.5 GW of Virginia gas as turbines secured. An adverse ruling on Chesterfield would not remove the need the SCC found — 'an imminent reliability threat', per the order as reported — but it would push the answer toward purchased capacity, storage and the third-party dispatchable RFP.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the NextEra combination changes the buyer more than the docket. Basis: the merger release keeps Dominion Energy Virginia's president in place and Blue as president and CEO of regulated utilities, and the SCC, NCUC, South Carolina, FERC and NRC approvals leave Virginia's rate proceedings, IRP cycle and RFP calendar intact; but the combined company's capital allocation, supplier qualification and framework agreements would sit with NextEra, whose merchant subsidiary is the largest developer of storage in this corpus. We expect procurement platforms to migrate after the second-half-2027 close and Virginia's regulatory calendar not to. This is inference from the release and the Utility Dive coverage, not a stated plan.

(Low confidence) We assess that CVOW's remaining risk is now shareholders' rather than customers' and that this disciplines the schedule more than any regulatory deadline. Basis: the 10-K's cost-sharing bands (50 percent recovery between $10.3B and $11.3B, none between $11.3B and $13.7B), a budget at $11.65B, a $58M non-GAAP benefit in Q1 2026 for costs 'not expected to be recovered from customers', and a final-turbine date that moved from end-2026 to year-end 2027 in two quarters. Whether tariffs effective in April 2026 and the litigation with Interior produce a further revision is not knowable from the record.

INDICATORS TO WATCH. October 30, 2026 (expected, not company-confirmed) — Q3 2026 results: the ESA tranche above 12.0 GW and connections on pace for 13 would confirm Judgment 1's conversion rate; a flat ESA figure with a rising headline would not. November 17, 2026 — SCC evidentiary hearing on the merger (Case PUR-2026-00112), with a final order expected January 29, 2027: conditions on data-center cost allocation would show the docket outlasting the buyer (Judgment 6). December 18, 2026 — Dispatchable Generation RFP bids due: storage or hybrid winners would open the third lane Judgment 5 anticipates. January 1, 2027 — GS-5 effective: a surge of ESAs signed in Q4 2026 under existing terms would show the tariff's filter working before it applies. About October 29, 2026 — the amended line-extension policy with mandatory contributions in aid of construction, due 90 days after the July 31 order. The next comprehensive IRP (an even-numbered-year filing per the company's cadence) — the storage total against the 4 GW-by-2030 statute (Judgment 4). The Supreme Court of Virginia's decision on Chesterfield (Judgment 5). Year-end 2026 — the third CVOW offshore substation; year-end 2027 — the final turbine (Judgment 7). March 2027 — the third biennial review filing.

relationships.note: Amazon and Dominion Energy Virginia signed a memorandum of understanding in October 2024 to explore development and financing structures for one or more SMRs at North Anna.

The company's October 16, 2024 release says the MOU 'documents … efforts to jointly explore innovative ways to advance SMR development and financing while also mitigating potential cost and development risks for customers and capital providers', with Robert Blue calling it 'a potential path to advance SMRs with minimal rate impacts for our residential customers' and Amazon's Kevin Miller stating that nuclear 'can help meet the energy needs of our customers for decades to come'. The 2025 IRP Update records that the company 'continues to explore opportunities for innovative financial partnerships with third parties and high load customers, which may provide avenues for earlier deployment of SMRs', and the July 2026 Early Site Permit renewal keeps the site available; no binding agreement, unit count or supplier had been announced by September 2026. relationships.scale: 0.8138 NextEra shares plus a pro rata share of $360M cash per Dominion share; NextEra 74.5% / Dominion 25.5%
relationships.note: NextEra Energy, the parent of NextEra Energy Resources, agreed on May 15, 2026 to acquire Dominion Energy in an all-stock combination expected to close in the second half of 2027.
relationships.context:
The May 18, 2026 joint release sets the exchange ratio at 0.8138 NextEra shares per Dominion share plus a one-time aggregate cash payment of $360 million, pro forma ownership of approximately 74.5 percent and 25.5 percent, a combined company of approximately 10 million customer accounts, 110 GW of generation and $138 billion of rate base, John Ketchum as chairman and CEO, Robert Blue as president and CEO of regulated utilities, Edward Baine as president and CEO of Dominion Energy Virginia, dual headquarters in Juno Beach and Richmond and a board of ten NextEra and four Dominion directors. Applications were filed July 15, 2026 with the SCC (Case PUR-2026-00112, hearing November 17, 2026), the NCUC, the South Carolina PSC, FERC and the NRC, with $2.25 billion of shareholder-funded bill credits over two years post-close.

The covered dossier is NextEra Energy Resources, the merchant development subsidiary; the acquirer is its parent. For this corpus the consequence is that the largest regulated data-center utility and the largest storage developer would share an owner from late 2027.

policyExposure.exposure: The DOM Zone cleared at the RTO price cap in consecutive auctions — $329.17/MW-day for 2026/2027 and $333.44/MW-day for 2027/2028, the latter with a 14.4 percent reserve margin against a 20 percent target and forecast load up 5,249.9 MW 'largely due to additional Large Loads' (PJM report). The 2025 IRP Update calls the 2026/2027 result 'the second-highest capacity price ever for the DOM Zone'; the cost passes to customers through fuel and purchased-power riders and was cited by the SCC in certifying the Chesterfield plant.
policyExposure.mitigation: The GS-5 class's 60 percent generation minimum and the company's self-build gas program (CERC 2029; CCGTs 2032–2034) are the company's stated responses; PJM's cap-and-floor collar applies for the 2026/2027 and 2027/2028 delivery years only.

policyExposure.regime: Virginia large-load cost allocation (GS-5; Rider T-1 direct assignment; HB 1393; 2026 budget consumption tax)
policyExposure.exposure: The SCC's November 2025 order created the GS-5 class effective January 1, 2027 and ordered alternative cost-allocation proposals for generation and transmission; its July 31, 2026 Rider T-1 order requires direct assignment of defined transmission facilities to data centers through mandatory contributions in aid of construction. The 2026 General Assembly considered 61 data-center bills and sent 15 to the Governor, including HB 1393 on allocating generation-expansion costs to customers of 25 MW or more; the budget signed June 30, 2026 imposes a $0.011/kWh electricity consumption tax on data centers from July 1, 2026 (capped at $600M a year, sunsetting June 30, 2028) while keeping the sales-tax exemption.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company's own tariff proposal — 14-year contracts, 85/60 percent minimums, enhanced collateral — was designed, per the 10-K, 'to minimize both cross-rate class subsidies and stranded costs'; the amended line-extension policy is due about October 29, 2026.

policyExposure.regime: Federal offshore-wind policy and import tariffs (CVOW)
policyExposure.exposure: The Department of the Interior suspended work on CVOW for 90 days on December 22, 2025; a preliminary injunction on January 16, 2026 allowed construction to resume. Tariffs effective in April 2026, revised PJM network-upgrade costs and updated installation projections took the budget to approximately $11.7 billion per the Q2 2026 10-Q, inside the band where the 10-K says incremental cost is unrecoverable from customers; the final turbine moved to year-end 2027.
policyExposure.mitigation: Litigation against the stop-work order; a $123M unused contingency; Stonepeak funds 48 percent of the remaining capital (Q2 2026 deck).

policyExposure.regime: Virginia Clean Economy Act and the April 2026 storage statute
policyExposure.exposure: The VCEA deems 2.7 GW of storage by 2035, 16.1 GW of solar and onshore wind by 2035 and 5.2 GW of offshore wind before 2035 to be in the public interest and sets a carbon-free path to 2045 (10-K); the April 2026 law raises storage to 16.0 GW of short-duration by 2045 (4.0 GW by 2030) and 4.0 GW of long-duration by 2045 (10-Q). The 2025 IRP Update's preferred plan carries 2,000 MW of storage and states it 'would require the Company to petition the Commission for a reliability exception outlined in the VCEA in order to preserve existing and planned fossil generation from retirement in 2045'; the Chesterfield certificate is under appeal on VCEA and environmental-justice grounds.
policyExposure.mitigation: Annual clean-energy petitions and RFPs execute the mandates; the reliability-exception petition is the company's stated route for keeping gas.

policyExposure.regime: FERC large-load and co-location rules (PJM, Docket EL25-49)
policyExposure.exposure: FERC ordered PJM on December 18, 2025 to create interim non-firm, firm contract-demand and non-firm contract-demand transmission services for large and co-located loads, with compliance filings in January and February 2026; PJM's 2026 forecast applies firm/non-firm vetting to large-load additions. No Dominion-specific provision was found; the rules govern how a data center could sit behind an existing plant on Dominion's system and what it would owe the grid.

Applications filed with the SCC (Case PUR-2026-00112; evidentiary hearing November 17, 2026; final order expected January 29, 2027 per the Q2 2026 deck), the North Carolina Utilities Commission, the South Carolina PSC (hearings December 8, 2026), FERC under Section 203 and the NRC (license transfers for the nuclear fleet); the release commits $2.25 billion of shareholder-funded bill credits over two years post-close, dual headquarters and employment commitments.
policyExposure.mitigation: Close targeted for the second half of 2027; Series C preferred to be redeemed if closing falls after January 2027 (10-Q).
